# Server test fixtures

These fixtures cover GTFS realtime parsing and security middleware persistence. For general patterns, start with the [server test guide](../README.md).

## File inventory

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`../fixtures.ts`](../fixtures.ts) | In-memory GTFS realtime protobuf generators for normal feeds, alerts, and parser edge cases. |
| [`loader.ts`](./loader.ts) | `loadFixture(id)` and collection helpers; reads `feeds/<id>.bin` first, then falls back to a generator for supported IDs. |
| [`generate-fixtures.ts`](./generate-fixtures.ts) | Writes synthetic and edge `.bin` files plus `feeds/manifest.json` from `../fixtures.ts`. |
| [`feeds/download-fixtures.ts`](./feeds/download-fixtures.ts) | Fetches current MTA feeds into feed-ID `.bin` files and rewrites the manifest; requires network access. |
| [`feeds/manifest.json`](./feeds/manifest.json) | Metadata describing the committed fixture set and how it was produced. |
| [`security.ts`](./security.ts) | Typed security table rows, standard data, low-level insert/clear functions, and scenario seeders. |
| [`middleware-helpers.ts`](./middleware-helpers.ts) | Migrated test databases, named scenarios, reset, row assertions, and synchronous transaction helpers. |
| [`middleware-fixtures-demo.test.ts`](./middleware-fixtures-demo.test.ts) | Executable examples of security database scenarios and assertions. |

## Binary feed inventory

All `.bin` files are GTFS realtime protobuf payloads. `gtfs*.bin` are saved feed-ID snapshots. `synthetic-*.bin` and `edge-*.bin` are generated by `generate-fixtures.ts`. The synthetic ACE, BDFM, G, JZ, and SI files currently reuse the B Division generator; their names identify loader/feed slots, not distinct route contents. Binary timestamps are fixed when generated, so use in-memory generators for cases that require current arrival times.

| Files under `feeds/` | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `gtfs.bin`, `gtfs-ace.bin`, `gtfs-bdfm.bin`, `gtfs-g.bin`, `gtfs-jz.bin`, `gtfs-l.bin`, `gtfs-nqrw.bin`, `gtfs-si.bin` | Saved payloads for matching subway feed IDs. |
| `synthetic-gtfs.bin` | Generated A Division trip updates. |
| `synthetic-gtfs-ace.bin`, `synthetic-gtfs-bdfm.bin`, `synthetic-gtfs-g.bin`, `synthetic-gtfs-jz.bin`, `synthetic-gtfs-si.bin` | Generated B Division structure used in those feed slots. |
| `synthetic-gtfs-l.bin` | Generated L line trip updates. |
| `synthetic-gtfs-nqrw.bin` | Generated N/Q/R/W trip updates. |
| `synthetic-alerts.bin` | Generated alert entities. |
| `edge-empty.bin` | Feed header with no entities. |
| `edge-unassigned.bin` | Unassigned train trips. |
| `edge-rerouted.bin` | Track mismatch indicating a reroute. |
| `edge-past-arrivals.bin` | Arrivals in the past for filtering tests. |
| `edge-deleted.bin` | Deleted feed entities. |
| `edge-no-nyct-extension.bin` | Feed without the NYCT header extension. |

`loadFixture("gtfs")` uses the disk snapshot if it exists; if absent, it maps to `synthetic-gtfs`. An edge ID similarly falls back to its in-memory generator. `hasDiskFixtures()` checks for the manifest only; use `loadFixture` when a test needs a specific payload.

```ts
import { expect, it } from "vitest";
import { loadFixture, loadFixtures } from "./loader.js";

it("loads feed edge cases", () => {
  const empty = loadFixture("edge-empty");
  const cases = loadFixtures(["edge-unassigned", "edge-rerouted"]);
  expect(empty.length).toBeGreaterThan(0); // Header-only protobuf still has bytes.
  expect(cases.get("edge-rerouted")?.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
});
```

## Security database scenarios

The security fixtures seed the `security_*` tables created by application migrations. Choose the smallest scenario that exercises the behavior:

| Scenario | Helper | Intended case |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `standard` | `createTestDatabaseWithFixtures()` | All standard security data, including five API keys. |
| `auth` | `createAuthTestDatabase()` | One valid read-only key. |
| `authorization` | `createAuthorizationTestDatabase()` | Read, write, and admin scopes. |
| `password-reset` | `createPasswordResetTestDatabase()` | Valid, expired, and used tokens plus reset attempts. |
| `rate-limit` | `createRateLimitTestDatabase()` | Bans, trusted IPs, and related keys. |
| `security-events` | `createSecurityEventTestDatabase()` | Events, notification preferences, and history. |
| `account-lockout` | `createAccountLockoutTestDatabase()` | Locked accounts and password history. |

`createEmptyTestDatabase()` applies migrations without seeding. `createFileBasedTestDatabaseWithFixtures()` returns `{ db, cleanup }` for persistence tests; call `cleanup()` in `finally`. `resetToScenario(db, name)` clears and reseeds an existing connection. `setupMiddlewareTestDatabase()` wraps setup and teardown for a suite. Table assertion helpers take the table name **without** the `security_` prefix.

```ts
import type Database from "better-sqlite3";
import { afterEach, beforeEach, expect, it } from "vitest";
import {
  assertSecurityTableRowCount,
  createAuthorizationTestDatabase,
  getSecurityTableRows,
} from "./middleware-helpers.js";

let db: Database.Database;
beforeEach(async () => {
  db = await createAuthorizationTestDatabase();
});
afterEach(() => db.close());

it("has three permission levels", () => {
  assertSecurityTableRowCount(db, "api_key_registry", 3);
  const scopes = getSecurityTableRows(db, "api_key_registry").map((row) => row.scope);
  expect(scopes).toEqual(expect.arrayContaining(["read", "write", "admin"]));
});
```

`withTestTransaction(db, callback)` always rolls back. `withSavepoint(db, callback)` releases changes on success and rolls back on throw. Both callbacks must be synchronous: an async callback would finish the savepoint before its promise settles.

## Adding a fixture

For a parser case, add an in-memory generator in `../fixtures.ts`, register its ID in `loader.ts`, and add a `generate-fixtures.ts` definition if a binary should be committed. Regenerate the binary and manifest together, then document the new file above. For a security case, add typed rows and a seeder in `security.ts`, expose a named scenario in `middleware-helpers.ts` if it will be reused, and document it here. Keep test data deterministic and close each database connection.
